cases.name: equal_ascii
cases.note: both sides decode to the ASCII string "hello-world"

cases.name: not_equal_same_length
cases.note: "hello-world" vs "hello-worle" -- same length, differs in the last byte

cases.name: not_equal_different_lengths_shorter_first
cases.note: "sec" vs "secret-value" -- a is a prefix of b, different lengths

cases.name: not_equal_different_lengths_longer_first
cases.note: "secret-value" vs "sec" -- b is a prefix of a, different lengths

cases.name: non_ascii_equal
cases.note: UTF-8 "你好" + a NUL byte + 0xff + 0x7f + 0x80 + an emoji's bytes; identical on both sides

cases.name: non_ascii_not_equal_last_byte
cases.note: same bytes as non_ascii_equal, but the final byte differs (0x80 vs 0x81)

cases.name: not_equal_would_be_equal_case_folded
cases.note: "SECRET-VALUE" vs "secret-value" -- equal only if case-folded; proves no case-folding happens

cases.name: a_over_limit
cases.note: a is 4097 bytes of 0x61 ('a'), one byte over gate::MAX_INPUT_LEN (4096); rejected regardless of b

cases.name: b_over_limit
cases.note: b is 4097 bytes of 0x61 ('a'), one byte over gate::MAX_INPUT_LEN (4096); rejected regardless of a

cases.name: both_exactly_at_limit_equal
cases.note: both sides are exactly gate::MAX_INPUT_LEN (4096) bytes of 0x61 ('a'); at the limit, so this must still compare rather than error

cases.name: both_exactly_at_limit_not_equal
cases.note: both sides are exactly gate::MAX_INPUT_LEN (4096) bytes, but of different byte values (0x61 vs 0x62); still compares rather than erroring
